Definition: probably akin to the base of G1150 (through the idea of violence); detriment:--damage, loss.
BiblicalUsage: Loss is the word's whole meaning, and Paul gives it its sharpest edge. In Acts 27 the sailors face ‘damage and much loss’ when they ignore Paul's warning about sailing on, and in Philippians 3 Paul counts everything he once prized as loss beside knowing Christ. The word covers both kinds of loss at once: what a storm takes, and what a person willingly gives up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's counting is the heart of the gospel's arithmetic. What the world calls gain — status, pedigree, achievement — he calls loss, because none of it can stand next to Christ. My position is simple: whatever I have to lose to gain Him is no loss at all.
